title: Service adapters behind typed capabilities; no arbitrary service/action/parameter endpoint and no operator-supplied IAM JSON bypass
why_open: The Studio talks to exactly one AWS service. `apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts:69` constructs the only client in the app (`new DynamoDBClient({ endpoint: process.env.AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_DYNAMODB || undefined })`), and `apps/system-studio/package.json:14-16` declares exactly two AWS SDK packages (`@aws-sdk/client-dynamodb`, `@aws-sdk/lib-dynamodb`). A repo-wide grep for `client-sts|client-ecs|client-rds|client-cloudfront|client-acm|client-cost-explorer|client-budgets|client-resource-groups` matches only two ledger `.md` files — no ECS, RDS, CloudFront, ACM, S3, SQS, SES, Lambda, Cost Explorer, Budgets or Tagging client exists anywhere in the tree. The one surface that claims to show running infrastructure, `apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:337-414` ('AWS estate'), renders entirely from `apps/system-studio/src/generated/platform-truth.json`, whose `estate.generatedAt` is `2026-07-31T23:40:04.289Z` — a hand-run inventory snapshot, not a live read (`docs/architecture/aws-current-state.md:3-4` says so: 'Generated ... by tools/aws-inventory.mjs, run from .github/workflows/aws-inventory.yml'). There is no capability type, no adapter module, no per-surface refresh cadence, no server-side cache, no backoff, and — the load-bearing gap — no distinction between 'empty list' and 'AccessDenied' anywhere: `listTenants` at `registry.ts:207` does `(out.Items ?? [])`, the exact shape STUDIO-000-007 forbids for a call that could have failed. NOTE the constraint that decides the design: `tests/architecture/forbidden-clients.test.mjs:344-370` forbids any AWS SDK import outside `OWNERS.aws`, which at `:198-207` names only `apps/web/src/lib/s3.ts` and `apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts`, and `:464` asserts `AWS_EXEMPT.size === 0`. New adapters must be added as OWNERS, never as exemptions.
smallest_real_change: One new owning adapter directory, `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/`, with `server-only` at the top of every module exactly as `registry.ts:1` does. (1) `client.ts` builds every SDK client from ONE factory that passes NO credentials and NO region literal — the default provider chain and the SDK's own region resolution, so swapping GitHub Action secrets or moving accounts needs no code change; `tests/security/no-hardcoded-estate.test.mjs:32,43` already scans `apps/system-studio/src` and will red on a `us-east-1` literal, so this is enforced today. (2) `capabilities.ts` declares a CLOSED union `type Capability = 'ecs:ListServices' | 'ecs:DescribeServices' | 'rds:DescribeDBInstances' | 'cloudfront:ListDistributions' | 'acm:ListCertificates' | 's3:ListBuckets' | 'sqs:ListQueues' | 'lambda:ListFunctions' | 'sts:GetCallerIdentity'` plus `type Reading<T> = { state: 'ok'; items: T[]; asOf: string; ttlMs: number } | { state: 'unknown'; capability: Capability; principalArn: string | null; awsErrorCode: string; minimumStatement: { Effect: 'Allow'; Action: string[]; Resource: string } } | { state: 'throttled'; retryAfterMs: number; asOf: string }` — a discriminated union with NO 'empty' arm, so a denied call structurally cannot be rendered as an empty list. (3) `inventory.ts` wraps each call in one `read<T>(capability, fn)` helper that maps `AccessDenied`/`AccessDeniedException`/`UnauthorizedOperation` to the `unknown` arm carrying the principal ARN from the identity read, `ThrottlingException`/`TooManyRequestsException`/`RequestLimitExceeded` to `throttled` with exponential backoff, and holds a per-capability in-process cache keyed by capability with a NAMED per-surface TTL constant (`ECS_TTL_MS = 15_000`, `RDS_TTL_MS = 120_000`, `ACM_TTL_MS = 3_600_000`) rather than one global number. (4) Register the new modules in `tests/architecture/forbidden-clients.test.mjs` `OWNERS.aws` (`:198-207`) with a stated reason, and add them to the `proof` list at `:396-402` so deleting the adapter reds the suite; do NOT touch `AWS_EXEMPT` (`:284`, asserted size 0 at `:464`). (5) Add the SDK packages to `apps/system-studio/package.json` and run `npm install --package-lock-only` — `tests/architecture/lockfile-knows-every-workspace.test.mjs` exists precisely because a missing lock entry kills every CI job on its first step. (6) Grant the read actions on `infrastructure/studio/iam.tf`'s task role (today `dynamodb.tf` grants six DynamoDB actions and nothing else). MUTATION PROOF, on the PRODUCTION render path not the helper: a stand-in client that throws `{ name: 'AccessDeniedException' }` must make the estate page emit the words 'unknown' and the minimum IAM statement; the SAME stand-in returning `{ services: [] }` must emit 'none'; delete the AccessDenied branch so it falls through to `[]` and the first test must red.

title: AWS authority split by account and capability; no browser or general application role has organization-wide administrator power
why_open: Two halves, both open. (a) NOTHING discovers or displays the identity in use. `sts:GetCallerIdentity` appears nowhere in the repository. The only place an account is shown is `apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:341-343`, `account {estate.account} · {estate.region}`, read from the static `platform-truth.json` — and the account id there is deliberately MASKED (`docs/architecture/aws-current-state.md:8`, 'Account `1549…97`', masked because the repo is public). So a developer opening the Studio cannot see which account they are looking at, which is the exact property this cluster is meant to deliver. Region comes from `infrastructure/studio/ecs.tf:56` (`AWS_REGION` from a Terraform var) and PARTITION is never expressed at all — `infrastructure/studio/dynamodb.tf` and `infrastructure/oidc/roles.tf` hardcode `arn:aws:` throughout, which is the same class of assumption REVIEW-FINDINGS/GE-010-007 calls a data-residency defect. (b) Nothing ASSERTS the authority split. `infrastructure/studio/iam.tf:39-43` creates the task role with a comment saying it is 'deliberately empty'; `infrastructure/studio/dynamodb.tf` then attaches six DynamoDB actions to it. There is no test that the Studio's task role stays free of `*:*`, `Resource = "*"` Allow, `iam:*`, `organizations:*` or an AdministratorAccess attachment — `tests/security/oidc-trust.test.mjs:184-224` does exactly that job for the three OIDC roles and has no counterpart for the ECS task role that the new AWS reads will widen.
smallest_real_change: `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/identity.ts` exporting `resolveIdentity(): Promise<Identity | Unknown>` that calls `STSClient.send(new GetCallerIdentityCommand({}))` through the shared factory, and derives EVERY estate fact from the answer rather than from a constant: `accountId` and `arn` from the response, `partition` parsed out of the ARN's second segment (`arn:aws-us-gov:...` -> `aws-us-gov`), `region` from `await client.config.region()`. Cache it for the process lifetime keyed by nothing (identity does not change under a task) but re-resolve on any AccessDenied so a rotated role is picked up. Render it in a persistent header band on the new estate page — account id, ARN, region, partition, and the `as of` — because 'which account am I looking at' must be answerable without scrolling. Then the guard: new `tests/security/studio-task-role-is-narrow.test.mjs` parsing `infrastructure/studio/*.tf` and asserting (i) every `aws_iam_role_policy` attached to `aws_iam_role.task` has no statement with `Effect = "Allow"` and `Action` containing `"*"` or ending `:*`, (ii) no `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment` on `.task` references `AdministratorAccess`, `PowerUserAccess` or `IAMFullAccess`, (iii) every Allow action on the task role is a read verb (`List*`, `Describe*`, `Get*`) EXCEPT the six DynamoDB registry actions, named explicitly, so a mutation action added later has to be added to that list deliberately. MUTATION PROOF: add `"ecs:UpdateService"` to the task-role policy and the guard must red; add `Action = ["*"]` and it must red on a different assertion. For the identity half, mutate `resolveIdentity` to return a hardcoded `us-east-1` and the estate-page test asserting the rendered region equals the stand-in STS response's region must red.

title: Desired-versus-actual comparison, drift severity, ownership, safe remediation plan, ignore policy with expiry, and recurrence detection
why_open: No drift module exists. A case-insensitive grep for `\bdrift\b` under `apps/system-studio/src` returns only prose in comments (`globals.css:74`, `registry.ts:121,466`, `fleet-health.ts:28`, `tenants/[slug]/page.tsx:65`) and ledger titles inside `generated/platform-truth.json` — no code. The desired side EXISTS and is unused for this purpose: `apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts:252-253` reads back a `DeploymentManifest` and a `TenantRegistryRecord` per tenant, and `apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts:610-622` writes the deployment artifact at CONFIGURING/ACTIVATING. The actual side does not exist at all (see STUDIO-070-004) and neither does the attribution that would join them: a grep for `tenure:tenant` or `GetResources` across `infrastructure/` returns nothing, so no provisioned AWS resource carries a tenant tag today. There is consequently no severity scale, no owner field, no remediation plan, no ignore-with-expiry record and no recurrence counter anywhere.
smallest_real_change: `apps/system-studio/src/lib/aws/drift.ts` exporting a PURE `compareDesiredToActual(desired: DeploymentManifest, actual: Reading<TaggedResource>[]): DriftReport` — pure so it is testable without AWS, and taking the `Reading<T>` union directly so a denied read cannot be compared as 'the resource is missing'. `DriftReport` items carry `{ resourceKey, severity: 'serving' | 'costly' | 'cosmetic', owner: string, desired, actual: T | { unknown: Capability }, remediation: { safe: true; describe: string } | { safe: false; refusedBecause: string; awsCliCommand: string }, firstSeenAt, occurrences }`. The rule that earns the module: when `actual.state !== 'ok'` the item is severity `unknown` with NO remediation offered — 'we were not allowed to look' must never produce a plan to recreate a resource that already exists. Persist ignore records and the recurrence counter as new sort keys in the EXISTING registry table via `registry.ts:160 putTenantItemIfAbsent` (`sk = DRIFT#IGNORE#<resourceKey>` with a required `expiresAt`; an ignore with no expiry is refused at construction, because a permanent ignore is a deleted finding). Render on `apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/[slug]/page.tsx`, which already loads the deployment. MUTATION PROOF: feed a `{ state: 'unknown' }` reading for the ECS service and assert the report says unknown and offers NO remediation; delete that branch so unknown falls into the 'missing' path and the test must red. Separately, construct an ignore record with `expiresAt` omitted and assert it throws.

title: Step-up authentication and fresh authorization for production, high-cost, security-sensitive, identity, data export, lifecycle and destructive actions
why_open: There is no step-up anywhere. `apps/system-studio/src/lib/auth.ts:21-55` configures one Credentials provider with `session: { strategy: 'jwt' }` and a single `session` callback; nothing records an authentication INSTANT, nothing re-prompts, and no action checks the age of the session. The high-risk path proves it: `apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts:541 advanceState` calls `operator()` (`:64-73`), which only asks `isOperator(session.user.email)` — the same check a read page makes — and then advances a tenant all the way to irreversible `PURGING`. The second identity is free text: `actions.ts:549` reads `approvedBy` from the form and `:635` passes `approverIsOperator: approvedBy ? isOperator(approvedBy) : undefined`, so the requesting operator types any OTHER allowlisted address and the engine treats it as approval — that address's holder never authenticated. `apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/[slug]/AdvanceControls.tsx:63-87` renders `HighRiskConfirmation` plus an `approvedBy` email input and no typed confirmation of the target and no re-authentication. `apps/system-studio/src/components/states.tsx:249-285` requires five fields on the confirmation but none of them is a credential. This is the gate the AWS mutation surface must sit behind before any `UpdateService` or `CreateInvalidation` path is built.
smallest_real_change: (1) In `auth.ts`, add a `jwt` callback that stamps `token.authAt = Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)` on sign-in ONLY (`if (user)`), and surface it as `session.authenticatedAt`; without an authentication instant nothing downstream can be fresh. (2) New `apps/system-studio/src/lib/step-up.ts` exporting `requireStepUp(session, opts: { maxAgeSeconds: number; confirmation: string; expected: string; presentedSecret: string })` returning a discriminated `{ ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: 'stale-session' | 'confirmation-mismatch' | 'secret-rejected' }`. Freshness window as a NAMED constant per class — `LIFECYCLE_MAX_AGE_S = 300`, `DESTRUCTIVE_MAX_AGE_S = 120` — not one number. The typed confirmation is compared with the exact target string (the tenant slug for a lifecycle move, the service ARN for a scale change); the re-presented secret goes through the EXISTING `secretMatches` (`operators.ts:123`) so there is no second credential system. (3) Call it inside `advanceState` (`actions.ts:545`, immediately after `operator()`) for every transition where `REQUIRES_APPROVAL` in `packages/provisioning/src/lifecycle.ts` says so, and inside `configuration/actions.ts publish`; refuse with the typed reason rather than a generic error. (4) `AdvanceControls.tsx` gains a `confirm` text input labelled with the slug it must equal and a password input for the re-presented secret, both shown only when the transition needs them — server-side is the control, the UI is the courtesy, exactly as `:16-18` already says. MUTATION PROOF on the PRODUCER: in an action-level test, advance a tenant with a session whose `authenticatedAt` is 10 minutes old and assert the refusal is `stale-session` and that `advanceTenant` was NEVER called; then delete the `requireStepUp` call in `advanceState` and confirm the test reds. Second mutation: pass a confirmation string differing by one character and assert refusal.

title: Validate authentication, CSRF, scope, semantic authorization, separation of duties, expected version, schema, policy, budget, quota and idempotency at execution time — not only plan time
why_open: Roughly half of the list is validated at execution time and the rest is absent, and the absent half is the half that matters for a mutating AWS surface. What IS there: authentication (`apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts:64-73` re-checks the operator inside the action, with the right reason stated at `:57-63`), separation of duties (`:635 approverIsOperator`), and optimistic concurrency on the tenant STATE only (`apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts:495-497`, `ConditionExpression: '#s = :expected'`). What is NOT: no expected-VERSION on the payload — nothing hashes or compares the manifest/plan the approver saw against the one that executes, so `advanceState` recomputes `executeStep`/`deploymentManifest` from whatever `getTenant` returns at `:566` rather than from an approved digest; no idempotency of any kind — a double-submit produces a second real attempt (`registry.ts:505` writes `STEP#<at>#<attempt>`) or a `TransactionCanceledException` surfaced as 'this tenant moved while the page was open' (`actions.ts:644-649`), which is a race message, not idempotency; no budget or quota assessment even though `packages/finops/src/reporting.ts` `approvalFor`/`previewPlanCost` exist and the ledger admits at `docs/implementation/system-studio-aws-control-plane-execution-ledger.md:211-214` that they are 'published and computable but not yet enforced at execution time'. The contract to enforce against ALREADY EXISTS and the Studio does not use it: `packages/contracts/src/index.ts:215-226` defines `Command` with `expectedVersion` and `idempotencyKey` BOTH REQUIRED, `:573` `IdempotencyRecord`, `:611` `replayable(record, requestDigest)` — and the only caller in the repo is `apps/web/src/lib/commands/bus.ts:100 dispatch`, which the Studio cannot import (`tests/security/operator-plane-content.test.mjs` forbids depending on the cell app). `@tenure/contracts` is already in `apps/system-studio/next.config.ts:41 transpilePackages`, so the import path is open.
smallest_real_change: New `apps/system-studio/src/lib/command-gate.ts` exporting `gate<T>(raw: unknown, checks): Promise<Refusal | Proceed<T>>` that runs, in this order and all at execution time: `parseCommand` from `@tenure/contracts` (which enforces the semantic `Resource.Action` shape, a non-empty `idempotencyKey` and an explicit `expectedVersion`, refusing a missing one rather than defaulting); the operator check; the step-up check from STUDIO-020-008; an idempotency claim written into the EXISTING registry table via `registry.ts:160 putTenantItemIfAbsent` at `pk = TENANT#<slug>, sk = IDEM#<key>` carrying `requestDigest`, then `replayable(existing, digest)` from `@tenure/contracts:611` — same key + same digest returns the stored result, same key + different digest is a conflict, never a replay; and `approvalFor` from `packages/finops/src/reporting.ts` when the command carries a recurring-monthly estimate. Wire it as the FIRST statement of `advanceState` (`actions.ts:545`) and of `configuration/actions.ts publish`, with the form supplying `idempotencyKey` as a hidden field minted when the confirmation UI renders (so a double-click reuses it and a fresh page mints a new one) and `expectedVersion` as the tenant's current `digest`/`revision`. Add `@tenure/contracts` to `apps/system-studio/package.json` dependencies and run `npm install --package-lock-only`. CONSUMERS CHECKED for the shared-type risk: `Command` is constructed today only in `apps/web/src/lib/commands/bus.ts` and `packages/contracts/src/contracts.test.ts:122` — this change ADDS a construction site and does not alter the type, so no existing caller is silently widened. MUTATION PROOF on the PRODUCER: submit the identical FormData to `advanceState` twice and assert exactly ONE `STEP#` row is written and the second call returns the first result; then delete the idempotency claim and confirm the test reds. Second: submit the same `idempotencyKey` with a changed `to` state and assert a conflict refusal, not a replay.

title: Prove identical approved intent is idempotent and that stale/changed intent is rejected rather than overwritten
why_open: The 'rejected rather than overwritten' half is real on both write paths; the 'identical intent is idempotent' half is missing on both, and there is no test asserting either property end-to-end. Configuration publish: `apps/system-studio/src/lib/config-store.ts:66-74` writes at `configSortKey(record.revision)` and turns `ConditionalCheckFailedException` into 'Revision N already exists ... re-plan against the current revision' — correct rejection, but a RETRY OF THE SAME APPROVED PLAN hits exactly that error rather than returning the already-published revision, so the honest reading is that identical intent FAILS instead of being a no-op. Lifecycle: `apps/system-studio/src/lib/registry.ts:495-497` guards `#s = :expected` so a stale click is refused, but `:505` writes `STEP#<options.actor.at>#<attempt>` — two submissions a second apart are two different sort keys and two real `executeStep` runs (`apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/actions.ts:570`), one of which may deliver to the cell twice (`:576 deliverToCell`). No spec asserts any of this: `apps/system-studio/e2e/config-store.spec.ts` and `revisions-logic.spec.ts` exist, and neither submits the same approved intent twice.
smallest_real_change: Share the idempotency claim from STUDIO-060-002 rather than writing a second mechanism. In `config-store.ts`, on `ConditionalCheckFailedException` (`:70`) re-read the record at that revision and compare its content digest with the one being published: identical -> return the existing record as success (identical approved intent is a no-op); different -> keep today's refusal message verbatim. In `advanceTenant` (`registry.ts:462`), take the `idempotencyKey` through `AdvanceOptions`, write the claim in the SAME `TransactWriteCommand` as the STATE and STEP puts (`:477-523`) with `attribute_not_exists(pk)` on the claim item, so a duplicate submission fails the whole transaction atomically and the action returns the first outcome instead of running `executeStep` a second time. Then the proof, which is the actual deliverable of this item: new `apps/system-studio/e2e/idempotent-intent.spec.ts` driving the real UI — publish a configuration, resubmit the identical approved plan, assert one revision exists and the page shows success; then edit one value, resubmit against the stale revision, assert the refusal names the current revision and the stored values are UNCHANGED. MUTATION PROOF on the PRODUCER: remove the digest comparison in `config-store.ts` so an identical republish errors, and the first case must red; separately drop the conditional from the transaction and assert two `STEP#` rows appear and the second case reds.

title: Current-state gap report with severity, exploit/failure scenario, affected resources/tenants, target control, remediation phase and evidence
why_open: A gap report exists in name only. `apps/system-studio/src/generated/platform-truth.json` carries `findings` as objects of exactly two fields — `{ "finding": "No AWS Organization — a single-account estate", "owner": "GE-010" }` — and `apps/system-studio/src/app/platform/page.tsx:319-334` renders them as a two-column table headed 'Finding | Owner'. Six of the seven required attributes are absent: no severity, no exploit/failure scenario, no affected resources, no affected tenants, no remediation PHASE distinct from the owning item id, and no evidence link. `docs/architecture/aws-current-state.md` has the same shape in prose — it names gaps ('No OIDC provider exists', line ~36) and attaches an item id, and nothing else. Nothing anywhere states what an attacker or an outage does with a given gap, which is the field that makes the report actionable. The estate half is also silently stale: `estate.generatedAt` is `2026-07-31T23:40:04.289Z` and `platform/page.tsx:345-349` renders it as a bare date with no staleness treatment — the only staleness check on the page (`:98-106`) fires on a COMMIT mismatch, which says nothing about an inventory that has not been re-run for a week.
smallest_real_change: Give the finding a real type and make the compiler refuse a thin one. In `tools/platform-truth.mjs`, change the findings source from a two-field literal to `{ id, severity: 'critical'|'high'|'medium'|'low', finding, scenario, affectedResources: string[], affectedTenants: string[] | 'all' | 'none', targetControl, remediationPhase, evidence: { path, line? } }` and THROW at generation time when any field is missing or `scenario` is under ~40 characters — a generator that emits a blank column is how the two-field version survived. Author the seven or eight real findings from `docs/architecture/aws-current-state.md` (no Organization, no OIDC provider for 14 workflows, no Cognito pool, no backup vault, zero NAT with public-subnet tasks, unallocatable cost with no `tenure:tenant` tag, empty Studio task role vs the reads this cluster adds), each with the concrete failure sentence. Render as a severity-ordered table in `platform/page.tsx:319-334`, with the scenario as the row's second line so it cannot be dropped by a narrow viewport — and keep it inside an `overflow-x: auto` container, since `e2e/layout.spec.ts:133-173` fails a wide table that is not. Add an `asOf` + staleness badge driven off `estate.generatedAt` using the existing `StaleState` component (`components/states.tsx`, already imported at `platform/page.tsx:8`) with a NAMED threshold constant. MUTATION PROOF: strip `scenario` from one finding in the source and assert `node tools/platform-truth.mjs` exits non-zero; then assert the rendered page contains that finding's scenario text, and delete the second render line to confirm the e2e reds.

title: Read-only authenticated audit of every reachable route, role, tenant state, error state, viewport and theme
why_open: The audit exists but its route list is hand-written and demonstrably incomplete, so 'every reachable route' is false today and will get worse the moment this cluster adds AWS pages. `apps/system-studio/e2e/layout.spec.ts:40` hardcodes `ROUTES = ['/', '/tenants', '/tenants/new', '/platform', '/platform/cost']` at three widths (`:41`, `[1440, 1180, 900]`). The app router has more than that: `apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/[slug]/page.tsx` and `apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/[slug]/configuration/page.tsx` are reachable operator pages and appear in NO layout run and NO contrast run. The theme axis is narrower still — `apps/system-studio/e2e/preferences.spec.ts:368` checks contrast on only `['/', '/tenants', '/platform']`, so `/platform/cost`, `/tenants/new` and both tenant sub-pages are never measured in dark, compact or increased-contrast. Error states are not audited at all: `apps/system-studio/src/app/tenants/error.tsx` and `loading.tsx` exist and no spec renders either. Nothing anywhere enumerates the router filesystem, so adding a route is adding an unaudited route, silently — which is exactly how a new estate page would ship unmeasured.
smallest_real_change: One shared `apps/system-studio/e2e/routes.ts` that WALKS `apps/system-studio/src/app` for `page.tsx` files, converts each to a URL, and resolves the one dynamic segment (`[slug]`) from the seeded registry tenant — plus an exported `ERROR_ROUTES` list of deliberately-broken URLs (an unknown slug, which must render the 404/error boundary rather than an unstyled crash). Import it in `layout.spec.ts:40` and `preferences.spec.ts:368` in place of both hardcoded arrays, so the layout and contrast axes cover the same complete set. Then the ratchet that makes it stay true: `route-census.spec.ts` asserts the discovered route count equals a checked-in number and fails with the new path named when it does not — a coverage list that can grow without anyone noticing is the defect being fixed, so it must be the assertion, not the input. Keep the existing sign-in helper; nothing here needs new credentials, and `layout.spec.ts:26-29` already refuses to run without `PLATFORM_OPERATORS`/`PLATFORM_OPERATOR_SECRET` from the environment, which is this requirement's 'never use credentials embedded in files or prompts' clause already satisfied. MUTATION PROOF: add a throwaway `src/app/platform/estate/page.tsx` that renders overlapping absolutely-positioned text; the layout spec must now fail on that route WITHOUT anyone editing the spec. Delete the filesystem walk and hardcode the old five, and that failure disappears — which is the proof the census is load-bearing.

title: WCAG 2.2 AA including zoom/reflow, touch targets, high contrast, RTL readiness and colour-vision safety
why_open: Most of this is genuinely done and two clauses are genuinely absent. Done: contrast is measured on the rendered page across eight theme/density/contrast combinations (`apps/system-studio/e2e/preferences.spec.ts:358-375`), the 24px target floor is a token held constant in compact (`apps/system-studio/src/app/globals.css:92,101`), reduced motion and the 120-220ms band are asserted (`preferences.spec.ts:340-349`), and neither theme uses pure black or white (`preferences.spec.ts:377+`). ABSENT: (a) RTL readiness — `globals.css` contains 11 physical-direction declarations (`margin-left`/`padding-right`/`border-left`/`text-align: left`) and ZERO logical properties (`margin-inline`, `padding-inline-start`, `border-inline-*`, `text-align: start`); `apps/system-studio/src/app/layout.tsx:18` emits `<html lang="en">` with no `dir` attribute and nothing can set one. (b) Zoom/reflow — WCAG 2.2 AA 1.4.10 requires no two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px, and the narrowest viewport tested anywhere is 900px (`apps/system-studio/e2e/layout.spec.ts:41`); the suite already asserts `document.documentElement.scrollWidth > clientWidth` at `:126-129`, so the machinery exists and simply is never run narrow enough.
smallest_real_change: (a) Replace the 11 physical declarations in `globals.css` with their logical equivalents (`margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline`, `border-inline-start`, `text-align: start/end`) and add `dir={dir}` to the `<html>` element at `layout.tsx:18`, sourced from the same no-flash preference script that already sets `data-theme`/`data-density`/`data-contrast` — 'readiness' means the layout does not break when `dir="rtl"` is set, not that a translation exists. (b) Add `320` to `WIDTHS` in `layout.spec.ts:41`; the existing horizontal-scroll assertion at `:126-129` and the spill check at `:133-173` then enforce reflow for free, and any table that fails is fixed by putting it in the `overflow-x: auto` container `globals.css` already defines for `table.grid` (which `:143-151` documents at length). MUTATION PROOF: add a `test('layout survives RTL')` that sets `document.documentElement.dir = 'rtl'` and re-runs the existing overlap detector on every route; revert one `margin-inline-start` back to `margin-left` and that test must red while every LTR test stays green. For reflow, revert `WIDTHS` to three entries and the 320px failures must disappear — showing the new width, not a new assertion, is what catches it.

title: CSP, secure headers, CSRF, XSS/output encoding, SSRF egress policy, upload scanning, content-type verification, size/quota limits and safe file rendering
why_open: Six headers are set and the most important one is not. `apps/system-studio/next.config.ts:4-13` lists HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and X-Robots-Tag — there is NO `Content-Security-Policy` at any value, report-only or enforcing. The console renders an inline `<script dangerouslySetInnerHTML>` at `apps/system-studio/src/app/layout.tsx:27`, so a CSP added carelessly breaks the no-flash theme script; that is the reason it needs doing deliberately rather than the reason to skip it. SSRF egress policy is entirely absent and about to matter more, not less: `apps/system-studio/src/lib/deliver.ts` posts to `CELL_RECONCILE_URL` (`infrastructure/studio/ecs.tf:63`, an operator-supplied URL) with nothing validating the host, and this cluster adds a process that makes outbound AWS calls — a Studio that will fetch a caller-influenced URL is a Studio that can be pointed at `169.254.169.254`. `tests/security/no-host-derived-urls.test.mjs` exists but covers a different property (URLs derived from the request Host), not egress destinations.
smallest_real_change: (1) Add a `Content-Security-Policy` entry to the `securityHeaders` array at `next.config.ts:4-13`: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'sha256-<hash of NO_FLASH_SCRIPT>'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'`. Compute the sha256 of `NO_FLASH_SCRIPT` in `layout.tsx` at build time from the same constant that is rendered, so the hash cannot drift from the script — a hardcoded hash silently disables the theme script on the next edit. (2) New `apps/system-studio/src/lib/egress.ts` exporting `assertEgressAllowed(url: string): URL`, refusing anything that is not https, resolving the host and refusing RFC1918, loopback, link-local (`169.254.0.0/16`, which is the instance-metadata address and the actual SSRF prize) and IPv6 unique-local, and refusing any host not on an allowlist read from the environment. Call it at the top of `deliver.ts` before the fetch — one call site today, which is what makes it cheap now and expensive later. (3) New `tests/security/studio-csp.test.mjs` asserting the header exists, that `script-src` contains neither `'unsafe-inline'` nor `'unsafe-eval'`, and that `frame-ancestors 'none'` is present. MUTATION PROOF: add `'unsafe-inline'` to `script-src` and the guard must red; point `deliver.ts` at `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/` in a test and assert `assertEgressAllowed` throws, then delete the link-local branch and confirm that test reds. Verify the CSP does not break the app by running the Studio Playwright suite — a CSP that blocks the no-flash script shows up as a theme flash and a console error, not as a failed assertion, so `e2e/preferences.spec.ts` must be run and seen green.
